h1: The 6 Best Garden Carts and Wagons of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six garden carts and wagons, sorted by capacity, flatbed or dump design, tires, material and price tier.
summary: The Gorilla Carts 1000 lb steel utility cart is the best all round garden cart, with the highest capacity of the flatbed designs. The Gorilla 7 cu ft dump cart is the one to buy if you tip loads often, and the VEVOR 900 lb steel wagon is the value pick. The BILT HARD, VEVOR 500 lb and Gorilla poly carts suit lighter work.
intro: Most people shop garden carts by pounds, but the first decision is shape. A flatbed carries long, awkward items like plants, boards and bags, while a dump cart tips out loose material, and the wrong one turns every job into a chore.

Six carts were assessed here, relying on spec sheets and what owners report about daily yard work. We ranked them on capacity, flatbed or dump design, material, tires and price tier. We kept a spread of designs, so you can see where the tradeoffs sit, rather than six near copies.

products.name: Gorilla Carts Steel Utility Garden Cart, 1000 lb. Capacity, Gray
products.verdict: The highest capacity flatbed here, in sturdy steel.
products.description:
The Gorilla steel utility cart has a 1000 lb capacity and a steel build. It is the highest capacity flatbed design in this ranking.

It ranks first because a flatbed handles the widest range of jobs, from potted plants to firewood. It costs more than the VEVOR steel carts, in the $100 to $200 range, but offers the most capacity and a trusted name.

Buy it as the one cart that does most things. If you mostly move loose soil, a dump design is better.

products.name: Gorilla Carts Dump Garden Cart, 7 Cu Ft, 1200 lb Capacity, No-Flat Tires
products.verdict: The highest capacity cart here and the best for tipping loads out.
products.description:
This Gorilla dump cart has a 7 cu ft bed, a 1200 lb capacity and no flat tires.

It ranks second because it is the strongest cart on paper but a dump bed is less useful for awkward flat items than the flatbed above it. It sits in the $200 to $500 range, the priciest tier here.

Choose it if you move mulch, soil or leaves and want to tip the load rather than shovel it out.

products.name: VEVOR Heavy Duty Steel Garden Cart 900 lbs Garden Wagon Cart on Wheels
products.verdict: A steel wagon rated for 900 lbs at a much lower price.
products.description:
The VEVOR steel wagon has a 900 lb capacity and a steel build, priced in the $50 to $100 range.

It ranks third because it gives up some brand reputation and lists few features beyond capacity. What you gain is a high rating at about half the price of the Gorilla steel cart.

It suits budget minded buyers who want a strong steel wagon for general work.

products.name: BILT HARD 400 lbs 10" Rubber Tires Steel Garden Cart with 180° Rotating Handle and Removable Sides
products.verdict: A smaller steel cart with a rotating handle and removable sides.
products.description:
This BILT HARD cart has a 400 lb capacity, 10 inch rubber tires, a 4 cu ft bed, a 180 degree rotating handle and removable sides.

It ranks fourth because the capacity is lower than the larger carts. In exchange you get easy turning and sides that come off to make a flatbed.

Choose it for a small to mid size yard where flexibility matters more than raw capacity.

products.name: VEVOR Steel Garden Cart 500 lbs Heavy Duty Garden Wagon Cart on Wheels
products.verdict: The lowest priced steel wagon for lighter work.
products.description:
The 500 lb VEVOR is a steel garden wagon on wheels, priced in the $50 to $100 range.

It ranks fifth because the capacity is a step below the 900 lb version for little saving. It does cost among the least here.

Buy it if you want a simple steel cart for light jobs and do not need maximum capacity.
products.idealFor: Light jobs on a tight budget.

products.name: Gorilla Carts Poly Dump Cart, 2-Wheel Garden Wagon, 4 Cu Ft, 300lb Capacity
products.verdict: A light, rust-proof two wheel dump cart for small loads.
products.description:
This Gorilla poly dump cart has a 4 cu ft bed, a 300 lb capacity and a two wheel design. The poly body resists rust.

It ranks last because 300 lbs is the lowest rating here and two wheels are less stable than four. It is light and easy to move.

Choose it for frequent small loads in a small garden.

whatMatters.detail: A flatbed carries long or awkward items and is easy to load, while a dump bed tips out loose material. Pick the one that matches your most common job, because switching later means buying a second cart. Check whether the listing says dump or lists a tilt feature.
The pound rating is the structural limit and gets less useful as loads get awkward. Dense loads like wet soil weigh much more than they look. Compare the rating with your heaviest regular load.
Steel is strong but can rust if scratched, while poly resists rust and is lighter but can crack or fade. Pick by climate and how rough you are on the cart. Check the listing for the material.
No flat and rubber tires avoid punctures, while air filled tires ride softer. For a cart that sits in a shed, flat free tires save trouble. Look at the tire size and type.
Four wheels are steadier, and two wheels turn tighter. A two wheel cart behaves like a wheelbarrow and needs your lifting. Count the wheels in the listing.

faq.q: Do I need a dump or a flatbed cart?
faq.a: Dump for loose material like soil and mulch, flatbed for bags, plants and awkward items. If you do both, a flatbed with removable sides is a compromise.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a cart?
faq.a: Ignoring the design type. A high capacity dump cart is awkward for boards and pots.

faq.q: Is the Gorilla cart worth it over the VEVOR?
faq.a: The Gorilla offers more capacity and a known brand, while the VEVOR gives high rated capacity for less.

faq.q: How do I prevent rust on a steel cart?
faq.a: Rinse off soil, dry the bed and touch up scratches with paint before storing under cover.

faq.q: How do I assemble a garden cart?
faq.a: Most arrive flat packed. Set aside an hour, attach the wheels and handle and tighten all bolts.

faq.q: Can I use a garden cart on slopes?
faq.a: Yes with light loads, but see our hills guide for picks that handle slopes more safely.

finalTake: For most yards the Gorilla Carts 1000 lb steel utility cart is the best buy. If you move loose material, step up to the Gorilla 7 cu ft dump cart, and if you want value, take the VEVOR 900 lb steel wagon. The smaller carts suit light work.
